prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Make ONE original universal bone-remains sprite for a dark fantasy tactical game, on genuinely transparent background.
Authentic very simple low-resolution PIXEL ART. Design it as a 48x32 logical-pixel sprite with chunky square pixel clusters, enlarged with nearest-neighbor, only 6 flat colors: dirty ivory, gray-beige, taupe, muted purple-gray and charcoal shadow. Hard pixel steps and opaque color cells, no antialiasing, gradients, bloom, blur or soft alpha haze. Three-quarter overhead view and top-left light.
ONE low compact heap of SMALL BROKEN BONES of visibly varied shapes: short hollow tube ends, tiny thin splinters, short crooked fragments, small flat shards and knobbly joint chips. About 12 to 16 overlapping pieces. Most fragments 4 to 8 logical pixels long; none dominates the heap. Bone material must read, rather than rocks or gravel. Keep the overall pile low and broad with irregular silhouette, around twice as wide as tall.
No skull, jaw, teeth, recognizable human or monster skeleton, complete ribcage, intact long femur, large circular bone, upright plate, flesh, clothing, rocks, floor tile, pedestal, tray, ground patch, cast shadow outside the heap, text or watermark. No anatomy display, no neatly arranged separate specimens. All fragments belong to this ONE compact pile.
Specific design: A dense flattened oval, with short hollow-ended stubs embedded among slim diagonally crossing splinters; a few small flat chips fill the gaps. Very low profile, merged dark crevices only inside the pile.
layout: A dense flattened oval, with short hollow-ended stubs embedded among slim diagonally crossing splinters; a few small flat chips fill the gaps. Very low profile, merged dark crevices only inside the pile.
